rationale: unit:given.typing.focus and its dependencies introduce the type, positive-path domain, normalization, finite relative paths, and the concrete Box/Pair example. emptyPath requires well-formed input and a nonempty positive target, normalizes before and after, removes entries at or below the target, and inserts precisely one negative target entry. For each positive strict ancestor, remainingAfterMove follows the finite suffix of the moved path and emits positive entries for all siblings at each level. Other negative entries and incomparable positive branches are retained. Thus it implements the three authored steps without losing sibling information, and can empty a common prefix of several descendant entries. Valid paths cannot continue through an empty class. The exact nested Box result is also stated in supplemental empty_nested_path, which additionally checks a common-prefix move and rejection of unknown and already-empty targets. Root rejection matches the explicit nonempty-path scope; storage effects belong to later typing/operational judgments, not this type transformation.
limitations: General normalization correctness, including preservation of well-formedness/observations and idempotence, has not been supplied as a proved theorem; definitions are reviewed algorithmically on the authored well-formed domain.
